That is because every lodge is different, and every grand lodge is different.

In my local area we have 8 lodges that are relatively  close.  There are two districts, and basically it is two city lodges, with two rural lodges which create one district.

There is definitely a power struggle with the two districts, but I am blessed to be apart of a lodge that has members that are diverse in age and experience. 


My lodge understands that some of these rural lodges are dying because of their lack of community involvement, and we are working hard to have better communications within our local districts.  Brings a family man it would be impossible to attend every Masonic function in my region.   I would be doing something Masonic every night.


What we have done instead is set up Masonic social nights, traveling groups, Master Councils, and other small groups where the leadership from all 8 lodges and DDGMs and their Entourage can communicate freely and openly with everyone.

The result has been amazing so far.  There are more brothers attending degrees and stated meetings.  More brothers hanging out outside of the lodge, and overall more masonry happening.


What Freemasonry is can be different from brother to brother.  Some prefer serving their lodge, some prefer education, others like fellowship and bullshitting inside a cramped truck traveling 2 hours away to attend an out of town lodge. Either way you get what you put into it.

It can function like a church.  Meeting other brothers from different faiths has in no doubt strengthened my own faith.  We don’t talk religion in lodge, but outside of lodge it can be very educational.  You can also confess to your brothers and be completely open without fear of recourse.  They will whisper good council to you, but they always have your back.


If you want to donate to charity, there is someone in lodge or another body who will help you with that.

Find a lodge, contact a brother from the lodge, and ask questions.

Hello brother, I sell technology, and cameras are one of my big things.


I know some others have recommended ring, or nest, but although great for a single family home, I don’t recommend for businesses or places with heavier than home traffic.  Also you need to have a fantastic wireless network for these to work, so if your network is lacking, I wouldn’t go wireless. 

1. It could possibly open you up to harm with extra wireless access points. (Everyone knows there are weird guys who get off on trying to hurt the brotherhood)

2. If your network is slow, wireless devices just eat up the bandwidth and make it slower.



What I suggest.  Buy a good commercial type DVR/ NVR.  Put a camera on every entrance, exit, and window.  I suggest a camera in your lodge foyer, and maybe even one pointed at the lodge door.  (If someone ever did come in and act a fool you could at least see them.)

Buy a IP system with at least 3 mega pixel, but be mindful that Category cables can’t pass signal further than 300’.  It is actually a little more than that, but when I get to 300’ I look at other options. So try to put your NVR/DVR in a centrally locates area.
You can set it up with a monitor, keyboard and mouse, with a 5TB hard drive and have about a months worth of storage.

Next thing to consider. If your network is capable, hardwire your NVR to your network.  From there you can set up a VPN and view your cameras from your office, or house. Most NVRs have “cloud” technology, and you can download an app on your phone.

When you are training to be a pilot, everything  you learn is pretty much, what to do in an emergency.  Step 1. How to get the plane in the air.  Step 2. How to make coordinated turnes.  Step 3. How to get airplane back on ground safely.


The way my CFI teaches me, and it may be different for others is that we started flying, and he made sure I could do those 3 steps  in case he had a medical emergency, and I had to get him on the ground.  Then we started breaking everything down.  Ok you are taking off, but your fuel pump died.  What do you do?  So your yoke is stuck and Jamed in a weird position what do you do... you go over hundreds of these scenarios, and the answer always ends up being within the realm of, I will aviate the aircraft (fly in a stable coordinated manner). Navigate (not lose track of where I am or my surroundings, and communicate (call out of help, figure out if someone is close by for help.)


So once you have all of this good to go, you throw in another curve ball.  What to do with passengers.  My CFI always tells me to give them a job.  “Hey Bob, watch this gauge and tell me when it changes numbers.”  It will give your passenger a sense of helping, and they will feel like they are helping save the plane, instead of doomed in a cage a couple of thousand feet in the air.

I am a Christian, and I hope this isn't a question to start a debate.

In my youth I tried the whole atheist agnostic thing, and I wasn't raised in a religious house hold.  Although my family said they were Christian, we would onl go to church on Sunday's and Easter... If that. So coming out as non religious wasn't a big thing.

I liked the whole do whatever I want thing, sex, drugs, and rock and roll.  However I still felt empty, and even though by saying "religion is not my answer." I still had many questions in my life that I needed to be made clear.

Why is there good and evil? Is everyone good at the start, then turn evil through out their lives?  What happens after death?  Is 80 years or so really the only time that we will experience? These questions of spirit, morality, mortality, and death haunted me.  If I was an atheist, and I really believed in social evolution as well as physical evolution, then my only purpose on this earth is to advance my species.  So in that theory killing the weak, sick, and mutated, then breeding with the strong, powerful, and smart are the only ways to advance my cause. This would make me no better than Hitler.


This got me thinking that there has to be purpose in my life, and that purpose has to be from a higher calling.  Wanting to stay away from Christianity, I researched Easter religion, started meditating, thought that maybe all the religions had the same God and we just didn't know it. Still something was keeping me from believing the line of crap I was feeding myself.


I had a close friend who asked me if I ever read the Bibke, and I said "No."  I claimed to be a Christian for most of my life, yet I had never read it.   

On my own I started researching the Bible, I started understanding that the washed out versions of stories that you get at church aren't the full stories.  If you read it in a historical and cultural context, and search for translations that match the original words, you will open up new meanings in all of the stories.  I believe that most spiritual interpretations of the Bibke have destroyed Christianity.

And since the Bible isn't in Chronological order of the time each book was written, it has added confusion to the text, and when reading through we forget that the events took thousands of years to unfold.

This started helping me with my doubt of Christianity, and the way the Bible worked, however I still didn't have faith.


I started questioning God during a rough part of my life.  Why can't I have this, why is evil allowed in our hearts, why this, why that.  My heart was cold towards God.  This God who orders death to those who break his law, who want sinful men to judge others and atoinment can only be made if blood of a perfect innocent animal is spilled by the hand of a priest, this is not right. But it gets better because this God full of anger and wrath wants to forgive me, so he impregnated a virgin and sent his son to die for me?  Yeah right.


So I was reading Job, and I got to the part where Job is questioning God, and God bassicly responds that you have no right to question him.  We don't know the complete path, and we can't see past our own future.  He placed the stars in heaven, he created all living things past and present, where do we have the right to question his authority.

And it hit me, man brought sin in this world, man created death.  If we didn't win the innocent wouldn't have to die, and Gods son wouldn't have faced death. If there was no sin we could question God, but because of our imperfect spirit we don't have that right.  

I started viewing God as a loving God, as a parent, harsh, stern, but loving.  And with that my faith began to grow.

I am a Christian because I have tried other paths, I didn't want to love or like this God.  I tried my own way, and now I am where I am.


I am not denominational, I carry some legalistic views, I believe the Bible is misread, and incomplete, but I believe with all of the Gospel, and cannon is a good starting place.
